title: Bust Blasting
statementMd:
Charlie the CNC miller is a cad with a capital 'C'. He is going to clone a valuable statue of a famous voxel-based video game character, and you are going to help him.

The voxel shape is defined by three photos Charlie took, which have been traced into the form of simple, axis-aligned (but potentially concave) polygons representing front (𝑥𝑦xy), side (𝑧𝑦zy), and top (𝑥𝑧xz) views of the statue respectively.

The meaning of "axis-aligned" here is that every edge of every polygon is parallel with one of the 𝑋X/𝑌Y/𝑍Z axes.

Any 3-dimensional point not contained by all three polygon projections will be blasted out of existence leaving only the true form, which may consist of multiple pieces or no pieces at all.

![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/ac018eb42c5be1fe6eac1c18b4f07e7c39ec2c02.png)Illustration of a complex statue.

Calculate the volume of the final statue.

## Input

The input consists of three lines of input, each giving one view as a two-dimensional, axis-aligned polygon in anti-clockwise order, with integer coordinates measured in centimetres.

- First, the number of points, 𝑛𝑖ni (4≤𝑛≤1004≤n≤100).
- Thereafter, 𝑛𝑖ni pairs of integers 𝑢𝑖𝑗uij and 𝑣𝑖𝑗vij for all 1≤𝑗≤𝑛𝑖1≤j≤ni (−10000≤𝑢,𝑣≤10000−10000≤u,v≤10000).

It is guaranteed that for all adjacent vertices 𝑎a and 𝑏b, 𝑢𝑖𝑎=𝑢𝑖𝑏uia=uib or 𝑣𝑖𝑎=𝑣𝑖𝑏via=vib. No three consecutive vertices are collinear.

## Output

Output the integer total volume of the resulting shape(s) in cubic centimetres.
